Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rzig 1.0.0

rzig follows semantic versioning from this version on. The public interface is the exported R functions, the declarations of the Zig module rzig except rzig.internal, the markers and options of the Zig source, the Config/rzig/... fields of DESCRIPTION and the files rzig writes into a package. The README section “Stability” states the policy, including the supported Zig release series (0.16 and 0.17).

Since 0.2.3, the previous CRAN release, rzig has gained (details in the entries below):

  • a step-wise workflow: find_zig(), scan_exports(), render_bindings(), rzig_status(), build_zig(), test_zig(), create_rzig_package(), update_rzig(), install_zig() and zig_function();
  • types: logical values with NA, integer and logical matrices, complex and raw vectors, i64 and bit64 integer64, named lists, data frames, factors, sparse matrices, external values and classes;
  • R functions called from Zig, with R’s non-local exits resumed after the Zig cleanup;
  • R’s distributions, BLAS and LAPACK, optimizers and integration;
  • parallel reductions in a fixed order, random streams for worker threads, and interrupts and panics while worker threads run;
  • packages with C, C++ or Fortran sources, vendored C libraries, and Zig modules and C-callable functions shared between packages;
  • configure targets for the macOS version R was built for, Linux with musl and Windows on arm64;
  • eight vignettes with executable code.

rzig 0.42.4

Bug fixes

  • A string in the “bytes” encoding, which R cannot translate to UTF-8, gives an rzig error naming the argument instead of R’s translation error. The read methods of rzig.Sexp reject such strings with an rzig error as well and match list names in the “bytes” encoding by their bytes, so no R error leaves an exported function past its defer statements; unknown entries of a named list warn without printing the untranslatable bytes.

rzig 0.42.3

Bug fixes

  • rzig.parallelFor() and rzig.parallelReduce() return as soon as their worker threads finish. The calling thread waits on a condition variable that each worker signals when it ends, with a timeout of 10 ms for the interrupt check; it no longer sleeps in growing steps, which delayed every short loop by the remaining sleep (on Windows by at least one timer tick).

rzig 0.42.2

Bug fixes

  • The test package of the repository suggests bit64, which its integer64 tests use, and skips the worker-panic test under Valgrind as it skips the panic test of the calling thread.

rzig 0.42.1

Bug fixes

  • A test of create_rzig_package() expected the compiler step of rzig_status() to pass, which fails on machines without Zig, such as CRAN’s.
  • digest, the fallback of the Zig downloader for SHA-256 checksums on R older than 4.5.0, is listed in Suggests.
  • The vignettes load the packages they build through the build result, so R CMD check reports no undeclared packages.
  • CI checks the format of the Zig sources with Zig 0.16 only: the formatter of Zig 0.17 rewrites @intFromEnum and @enumFromInt into builtins that Zig 0.16 lacks. The README says so for package authors.

rzig 0.42.0

Documentation

  • inst/examples/poclp ships the case-study package of the article on rzig (sharp bounds on probabilities of causation by an exact linear program); a test assembles, builds and checks it.
  • A pkgdown configuration groups the reference and the vignettes, and a workflow publishes the site from the main branch.
  • A contribution guide and issue templates; the README lists packages that use rzig.

rzig 0.41.0

New features

  • Seven vignettes with code that runs: getting started, updating rzig in a package, exports and classes, threads and random numbers, numerical routines of R, code shared between packages, and distribution. The steps that need Zig run when a supported compiler is found.
  • Config/rzig/download-zig: true in DESCRIPTION lets configure download the pinned Zig release into the build folder of the package when it finds no compiler, for packages distributed through GitHub or r-universe; rzig_status() notes that CRAN does not allow it without its consent.
  • Methods of /// @class structs that return nothing return NULL invisibly, so m$add(x) prints nothing.

rzig 0.40.0

New features

  • rzig.parallelFor() and rzig.parallelReduce() run the indices in order on the calling thread in single-threaded builds, such as WebAssembly for webR, so that the framework compiles for wasm32-emscripten (CI cross-compiles it with Zig 0.16 and 0.17). Packages for webR are not yet supported: building them with webR’s toolchain is untested.

rzig 0.39.0

New features

  • configure compiles for the macOS version that R links for (MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, otherwise the minimum version of libR.dylib) in place of a fixed macOS 13.0, for Linux with musl (Alpine) as well as glibc, and for Windows on arm64 (from the name of R’s compiler). RZIG_ZIG_TARGET overrides the detected target.
  • CI cross-compiles the framework for these targets with Zig 0.16 and 0.17, and a canary job builds with Zig’s development version without failing the workflow.

rzig 0.38.0

New features

  • C-callable functions between packages: a package lists functions with callconv(.c) in pub const rzig_callables of its root Zig file, which rzig registers with R_RegisterCCallable() when the package loads, together with rzig_interface_version when it is declared. rzig.callable(ctx, F, package, name, .{ .interface = n }) loads the namespace of the providing package, fetches the function with R_GetCCallable() and checks the interface version.
  • The generated manifest names the R package (pub const package); document() regenerates it.

rzig 0.37.0

New features

  • Zig modules shared between packages: use_rzig_module() creates inst/zig/<module>/root.zig in the providing package, and use_rzig_import() adds <package>/<module> to Config/rzig/imports and the package to LinkingTo. configure resolves the module in the installed package with the new src/rzig/tools/imports.R and passes it to zig build; the importing package compiles it, so the packages share no code at run time. use_rzig_module() also writes inst/include/<package>_rzig.h, because R CMD check expects a package in LinkingTo to provide an include folder. The checks before compilation report imports that do not resolve, packages that LinkingTo does not list, and providers without an include folder.

Bug fixes

  • test_zig() failed with Zig 0.17, whose zig build has no --global-cache-dir; the global cache is now set with ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR.

rzig 0.36.0

New features

  • Vendored C libraries: src/rzig/c_libraries.zon lists C libraries whose sources the package ships; the template build.zig compiles them with Zig and turns each header into a Zig module (@import("name")) with translate-c, which works with Zig 0.16 and 0.17 (Zig 0.17 has no @cImport). Nothing is downloaded. use_rzig() writes the empty list, update_rzig() adds it when missing and never replaces it, and rzig_status() reports listed files that do not exist.

rzig 0.35.0

New features

  • Packages with C, C++ or Fortran sources: use_rzig(path, mixed = TRUE) and use_rzig_mixed(path) set Config/rzig/mixed: true, so that R compiles the sources of src/ with its own compilers next to the Zig library. The package’s own R_init_<pkg> registers its routines with rzig_register(), which adds the Zig routines; the checks before compilation report a mixed package whose sources do not call it.
  • use_rzig() without mixed = TRUE names use_rzig_mixed() when src/ holds other sources.

rzig 0.34.0

New features

  • rzig.Function receives an R function, and f.call(ctx, T, args) calls it from Zig with positional or named arguments and converts the result to T. An R error, an interrupt, or the exit of a condition handler or a restart outside the call returns rzig.Error; after the Zig frames have returned, R continues the error or the exit unchanged, so conditions keep their class and call and handlers outside the call run. Queued warnings come first, R’s random-number state passes to R and back, and R functions may call rzig packages again.
  • The objectives and integrands of rzig.Optimize and rzig.Integrate may call R functions; an R error of the routines themselves now reaches R as it is, without an additional rzig error.
  • src/entry.c contains rzig_unwind_run(), which stops R’s jumps with setjmp(); update_rzig() replaces an unmodified entry.c.

rzig 0.33.0

New features

  • rzig.parallelReduce() reduces over indices on worker threads in chunks fixed by the count alone, so the result (also a floating-point sum) is the same for every number of threads.
  • ctx.rngStreams() gives random streams for workers, seeded from R’s stream: index i always gets the same stream (stream(i), with uniform(), normal(), exponential()), so parallel draws follow set.seed() and not the number of threads.
  • A user interrupt while parallelFor runs stops the workers after their current index and is delivered as an R interrupt.

Bug fixes

  • A panic on a worker thread (for example a failed bounds check) used to call R from that thread, which could crash the session. The worker now records the message and ends, and the call raises it as an R error.

rzig 0.32.0

New features

  • rzig.Optimize.minimize() runs the optimizers of optim() (BFGS, Nelder-Mead, conjugate gradients, L-BFGS-B with bounds) on Zig objectives, with an optional analytic gradient and otherwise the central differences of optim(); the results and counts match optim().
  • rzig.Integrate.integrate() integrates a Zig function as integrate() does, on finite and infinite ranges, with QUADPACK’s failures as errors.
  • Errors in objectives and integrands are recorded and reported when the routine finishes; the routines run guarded against R errors.

rzig 0.31.0

New features

  • rzig.CscMatrix borrows a Matrix::dgCMatrix through its slots i, p and x and its dimensions; every index is checked on arrival (columns in order, rows inside the matrix and increasing within a column), so column(j) reads it without further checks. Other sparse classes are rejected with the as() call that converts them.

rzig 0.30.0

New features

  • rzig.Blas (gemm, gemv, syrk, trsm) and rzig.Lapack (potrf, potrs, getrf, getrs, gesv, geqrf, ormqr, gels, syevr, gesdd) call R’s BLAS and LAPACK with the shapes checked before each call, the call guarded, Fortran’s hidden string lengths passed, and LAPACK’s info turned into R errors. ctx.matrix(nrow, ncol) allocates a zero-filled rzig.MutableMatrix, and view() gives a read-only view.
  • use_rzig_lapack() sets Config/rzig/lapack: true, and the generated configure then links $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS); rzig_status() notes Zig code that calls them without it.

rzig 0.29.0

New features

  • rzig.Rmath.density(), rzig.Rmath.cdf() and rzig.Rmath.quantile() evaluate the d, p and q functions of R for 17 distributions (rzig.Distribution), with R’s parameter names and defaults (rzig.Rmath.Params(.gamma) is .{ .shape, .scale = 1 }), the tail and log options, and a guard that keeps an R warning turned into an error from jumping out of Zig code.
  • rng.draw(distribution, params) draws with R’s generator for the distribution, so draws match R’s for the same seed.

rzig 0.28.0

New features

  • Classes: a struct marked /// @class becomes an R class. init is the constructor, exported under the struct’s name (its arguments take /// @default), and each public function whose first parameter is the struct is a method, called as x$method(...). document() generates the $, print and .DollarNames methods, registers them in NAMESPACE (or through roxygen2 tags), and writes a help page with a Methods section. Methods may take ctx: *rzig.Ctx after the receiver. The objects are rzig.External values, so deinit runs when R collects them.

rzig 0.27.0

New features

  • rzig.External(T) keeps a Zig value in an R external pointer across calls: rzig.External(T).create(ctx, value) returns a new one, inputs give the value through .ptr, and R’s garbage collector runs deinit and releases the memory. The tag of the external pointer identifies the type and the package, so other objects are rejected without reading their memory; a value lost by saving and restoring is a clear error; a value created in a call that fails is released by the call.

rzig 0.26.0

New features

  • rzig.Sexp has read-only methods: kind() (an rzig.SexpKind), length(), isNull(), isObject(), isS4(), inherits(), attribute() (S4 slots are attributes), names() and classes() (copied into the call context), element() and field() for lists, and get(T, ctx), which converts the value by the rules of a parameter of type T.

rzig 0.25.0

New features

  • rzig.Record(T) reads a named list into the fields of the struct T by name (defaults fill missing entries, optional fields become null, unknown entries give a warning) and builds a named list from it as a result. A record carries any number of values in one argument.
  • rzig.DataFrame(T) reads the columns of a data frame into a struct of slices and factors, with its number of rows in .nrow, and builds a data frame with compact row names as a result.
  • rzig.Factor reads a factor (borrowed codes, copied levels) and returns one; codes outside the levels are errors.
  • ?T accepts NULL for every input type T, not only scalars.

rzig 0.24.0

New features

  • i64 and []const i64 read bit64::integer64 values (the 64-bit integers stored in the bits of a double vector of class integer64), and i64 also accepts integers and whole doubles up to 2^53 - 1 in absolute value. ?i64 maps NA and NULL to null; rzig.NA.integer64 is the missing value. i64 and []i64 return integer64 vectors.
  • Counts and indices of long vectors (beyond 2^31 - 1) reach Zig as i64; usize keeps the range of R’s integers, and its error message points to i64.

Behavior changes

  • f64, i32, usize, []const f64 and rzig.Mut([]f64) reject bit64::integer64 values, whose bits are not doubles, instead of reading them as wrong numbers.

rzig 0.23.0

New features

  • rzig.Complex (fields re, im; the layout of R’s Rcomplex) is a complex scalar, and []const rzig.Complex borrows a complex vector; toStd() and fromStd() convert to and from std.math.Complex(f64) for complex arithmetic. Both are also return types.
  • rzig.Raw holds the bytes of a raw vector in .data, borrowed as an input and copied as a result; []const u8 remains a UTF-8 string.

Repository checks

  • The scripts that copy the framework into the fixture, the example and inst/zig take the list of files from src/, so a new framework file reaches client packages.
  • The scaffold check follows the documented starter example (0.8.0) and the roxygen2 mode of document() (0.6.0); the fixture documents all its exports, so its R CMD check has no missing-documentation warning.

rzig 0.22.0

New features

  • []const rzig.Logical borrows a logical vector that can contain NA; rzig.Logical has the values .TRUE, .FALSE and .NA and the methods isTrue(), isFalse(), isNa() and fromBool(). []rzig.Logical returns a logical vector with NA.
  • []const ?[]const u8 copies a character vector in which NA becomes null, and []?[]const u8 returns one in which null becomes NA. ?[]const u8 accepts one string, NA or NULL.
  • rzig.NA.real, rzig.NA.integer and rzig.NA.logical are R’s missing values, for results that contain NA.

Bug fixes

  • Types written with a space before rzig., such as []const rzig.Logical, are recognized by the checks before compilation, and the printed export descriptions of scan_exports() name rzig.Mut(rzig.Matrix) and the other new types instead of calling them unsupported.

rzig 0.21.0

New features

  • rzig.IntMatrix borrows an integer matrix and rzig.BoolMatrix copies a logical matrix without NA; with rzig.Matrix they are views made by rzig.MatrixOf(T) with at(row, column) and column(j).
  • rzig.Mut([]i32), rzig.Mut(rzig.Matrix) and rzig.Mut(rzig.IntMatrix) duplicate an integer vector or a matrix before writable access; the duplicate keeps dim, dimnames and class and is what the R function returns. Writable matrix views add set(row, column, value).
  • rzig.Attributed(T) gains setMatrix(nrow, ncol) and setDimnames(row_names, column_names), checked against the dimensions before R allocates the result.
  • Matrices of the wrong storage mode are rejected with the storage.mode() call that converts them.

rzig 0.20.0

New features

  • ctx.print() and ctx.eprint() write formatted text to R’s output and message streams through Rprintf and REprintf, inside R_ToplevelExec, so a user interrupt noticed while printing becomes an R interrupt after Zig cleanup. Text of any length is written in full.
  • ctx.progress(total, show) returns an rzig.Progress bar on R’s message stream that redraws when its percentage changes and checks for a user interrupt at each redraw. A progress bar in the state of rzig.parallelFor workers is a compile error.

rzig 0.19.0

New features

  • The generated configure downloads Zig when no supported compiler is found and RZIG_DOWNLOAD_ZIG=true: the verified archive of install_zig() (Zig 0.16.0, or RZIG_ZIG_VERSION), kept in zig_home() for later installations. Without the variable nothing is downloaded, and the message for a missing compiler names the variable.

rzig 0.18.0

New features

  • install_zig() downloads a Zig release (0.16.0 by default, or 0.17.0) for the current platform into zig_home(), rzig’s user cache folder or the folder named by RZIG_ZIG_HOME. The archive is verified against the size and SHA-256 published in ziglang.org’s download index and pinned in rzig, and is fetched from a community mirror of Zig or from ziglang.org; an archive that differs is deleted before anything is extracted or run. uninstall_zig() removes the installations.
  • find_zig() and the generated configure scripts search zig_home() after the PATH, so a compiler from install_zig() builds rzig packages without further setup. Their messages for a missing compiler name install_zig().
  • New packages contain src/rzig/tools/fetch_zig.R, the downloader that install_zig() runs; update_rzig() adds it to existing packages.

rzig 0.17.0

New features

  • RZIG_OPTIMIZE=Debug in the environment of R CMD INSTALL, or build_zig(optimize = "Debug"), builds the Zig code without optimization and with the safety checks and complete stack traces of Zig’s Debug mode. ReleaseSafe stays the default; ReleaseFast and ReleaseSmall are rejected with a message, because the boundary turns failed safety checks into R errors. The printed build result names a Debug build.

rzig 0.16.1

Repository checks

  • The SIGINT integration check creates its readiness marker inside the tryCatch() that handles the interrupt, so a signal that arrives before the Zig loop starts is still caught on a busy machine.

rzig 0.16.0

New features

  • create_rzig_package() creates a new package in one call: a DESCRIPTION (GPL-3, SystemRequirements: Zig 0.16.x or 0.17.x, fields replaceable through fields), the scaffold of use_rzig() with the hello_zig() example and its help page, a testthat suite with one test, and optionally the workflow of use_rzig_ci(). The created package passes R CMD check --as-cran.

rzig 0.15.0

New features

  • use_rzig_ci() writes a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/rzig-check.yaml) that installs R and Zig and runs R CMD check --as-cran for each operating system and Zig version of its matrix (Linux, macOS and Windows; Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 by default), with the Zig tests of src/rzig/src/tests.zig first when that file exists.

rzig 0.14.0

New features

  • test_zig() runs the Zig tests of a package (zig build test) on the host without R: the test blocks of the files imported by src/rzig/src/tests.zig. The package folder receives no build output, the Zig cache is kept for the session, and failed tests are listed by name.
  • The build.zig template has a test step for test_zig(); update_rzig() installs it in packages with an unmodified older build.zig.

rzig 0.13.0

Behavior changes

  • Errors of the boundary name the R argument: “argument a of add_vectors must be a numeric vector; got integer; use as.numeric() in R” instead of “argument 1 of add_vectors must be …”. The names come from the manifest; a hand-written manifest without parameter names keeps the position.
  • The compile error for more than 32 arguments suggests passing related values together as one vector or matrix instead of a list argument, which the boundary does not accept.

rzig 0.12.0

New features

  • Export options on the marker line: /// @export name=<R name> gives the R wrapper a name other than the Zig name, and /// @export invisible makes it return its value invisibly; the options combine with internal.
  • /// @default <argument> <R expression> gives an argument of the wrapper a default value; the expression must parse and the argument must exist. The help pages show the defaults in their usage.

rzig 0.11.0

New features

  • zig_function() compiles Zig code from the R prompt into a package in the session’s temporary directory and defines its exported functions, the counterpart of Rcpp::cppFunction(); zig_source() does the same for a file and zig_eval() evaluates one expression of a given type. The header (std, builtin, rzig, the panic handler) and the registration block are added when the code lacks them, every pub fn is exported when the code marks none with /// @export, builds are cached for the session, and a compiler error is reported with the line of the code.
  • A knitr engine zig (eng_zig(), registered when knitr loads) compiles a chunk with zig_function(), so later R chunks call its functions.

rzig 0.10.1

Continuous integration

  • A CRAN-style check of a newly generated client package runs on Linux, macOS and Windows with both Zig series (tools/check_client_package.R): R CMD check --as-cran with two cores, the CPU-to-elapsed threshold of the installation and a separate temporary directory, failing on any NOTE.
  • A reverse-dependency job updates pnsbib from GitHub with update_rzig(), builds it and runs its native and R tests (tools/check_reverse_pnsbib.sh).
  • The R-devel job compares the R entry points the framework declares with tools:::nonAPI and tools:::funAPI() (tools/check_api_symbols.R).
  • rzig_status() of the example package must report every structural check ok, and the example lists its Zig sources for devtools::load_all().

rzig 0.10.0

New features

  • The environment variable RZIG_ZIG_CACHE names a persistent global Zig cache for the builds of client packages. Without it, each installation starts with an empty cache inside the package, which keeps R CMD check clean but lets Zig 0.17 compile its build runner again for every installation; with it, a repeated build of the starter package takes about 15 seconds instead of minutes on a loaded machine.

rzig 0.9.1

Tests

  • The integration check that sends a real SIGINT waits until R has entered the interruptible loop (R creates a marker file just before it), instead of sending the signal after a fixed 0.3 seconds, which a loaded machine could exceed before R started the loop.

rzig 0.9.0

New features

  • Exports in several files: the scan follows pub const name = @import("file.zig"); declarations of main.zig (recursively) and finds the /// @export functions of those files, registered as name.function. /// @export above pub const twice = other.twice; re-exports a function of an imported file. Before, markers outside main.zig were ignored without a message.
  • A marker in a file imported with a plain const, which the generated registration cannot reach, is an error that says how to import the file; a marked file that is not imported is noted by rzig_status(), and an R name exported twice is an error naming both places.
  • scan_exports() records the file of each export and the files scanned; print() shows the file of exports outside main.zig, and build_zig() attributes compiler errors in any of these files to their exported function.

rzig 0.8.0

New features

  • document() writes a help page man/<name>.Rd for every exported Zig function of a package that does not use roxygen2, from the function’s doc comment: the first paragraph is the title and description, and @param, @return, @examples, @details, @seealso, @references and @note fill their sections; code spans become \code{}. Pages rzig wrote for functions that are gone are removed, and pages of other origin are left alone. In roxygen-managed packages roxygen2 writes the pages, and rzig removes its own.
  • The starter hello_zig() documents its parameter and return value and has an example, so a new scaffold passes R CMD check without the “Undocumented code objects” and “No examples, no tests, no vignettes” warnings.
  • rzig_status() reports help pages that no longer match the doc comments.

rzig 0.7.0

New features

  • rzig.parallelFor() limits its worker threads: RZIG_NUM_THREADS lowers the number (an invalid value is an error naming the variable), OMP_THREAD_LIMIT is respected, and while R CMD check limits the cores (_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_, as in CRAN submission checks) at most two threads run. Before, a call used one thread per core up to 32 in any setting.
  • rzig.parallelThreadCount(count) returns the number of worker threads a call of parallelFor with count indices uses.

rzig 0.6.0

New features

  • Packages whose NAMESPACE roxygen2 generates: document() writes the useDynLib directive of the native routines into R/rzig-wrappers.R as a @rawNamespace tag and adds the lines roxygen2 writes from the tags to NAMESPACE, instead of a block that roxygen2::roxygenise() removed. The package works whichever of rzig::document(), roxygenise() or devtools::document() ran last; before, a call of roxygenise() after document() left .Call() without its native symbols (“object ‘hello_zig_’ not found”), which R CMD check reported only as a NOTE.
  • render_bindings() takes roxygen, and rzig_status() checks the bindings of both kinds of packages.

rzig 0.5.0

New features

  • A doc line /// @export internal marks a native routine that only the package’s own R code calls: it is registered and gets an R wrapper and a native symbol (<name>_), but the wrapper is not exported from the package and gets no help page. Packages no longer need to patch the generated manifest and NAMESPACE for such routines.
  • Only /// @export and /// @export internal are accepted; any other option, or a second @export line above one function, is an error of the scan with the file and line.
  • scan_exports() records internal, as.data.frame() shows it, and subsetting the result (exports[1:2]) keeps its class.

rzig 0.4.0

New features

  • update_rzig() brings a package to the installed version of rzig: it replaces the framework sources, updates every build file that is still an unmodified template of some rzig version (recognized by the MD5 sums of all templates rzig has shipped), adds missing build files, removes the Zig scanner that rzig 0.2 copied into src/rzig/tools/, and regenerates the bindings. Build files the package author changed are kept and listed; force = TRUE replaces them. The package author’s Zig sources and files rzig does not know are never changed or removed.
  • rzig_status(build = TRUE) takes lib, the library build_zig() installs into.

Behavior changes

  • use_rzig(overwrite = TRUE) no longer deletes the files under src/rzig that rzig does not know, and stops before changing anything when a build file differs from every rzig template; force = TRUE replaces such files. Before, it replaced customized build files and removed other files without a message.
  • rzig_status() recommends update_rzig() for framework sources from another rzig version.

rzig 0.3.9

Bug fixes

  • use_rzig() stops with an explanation when the package already has a hand-written src/Makevars or src/Makevars.win (which configure would overwrite and cleanup would remove, so that its settings silently disappeared from the built package) or C, C++ or Fortran sources in src/ (which the generated Makevars do not compile).
  • rzig_status() reports such sources and Makevars files in the Scaffold check. A source whose object file a customized src/Makevars.in lists counts as handled.
  • document() removes a useDynLib(<pkg>, .registration = TRUE, .fixes = "C_") line only when the old wrapper file shows that rzig 0.1 wrote it; a package author’s own directive stays in NAMESPACE.

rzig 0.3.8

Tests

  • The hostile-input suite (tests/abuse.R and the test package) passes S4 objects, an S4 class whose data part is a double vector, classed vectors (a units-like class and Date) and a data frame to every typed parameter and checks that each call ends in an R error naming the argument or converts the data part, and that rzig.Sexp returns the S4 object unchanged.

rzig 0.3.7

Bug fixes

  • Printing a column subset of a rzig_status object (for example status[, c("step", "ok")]) shows the data frame instead of failing with “non-character argument”.
  • build_zig() reports a duplicate-symbol error of the linker (duplicate symbol, multiple definition of) at the link step instead of the install step.

rzig 0.3.6

Compiler search

  • Without ZIG, find_zig() and the generated configure use the first compiler of a supported release series among the PATH and the usual install locations (~/.local/share/zig/*/zig, ~/zig/zig), so an old zig on the PATH no longer hides a supported one. When none is supported, the first compiler found is reported with the reason, and find_zig() lists the others. An explicit ZIG is used as given.
  • Development builds of Zig (for example 0.17.0-dev.12+abcdef) are rejected with a message saying so: their language and standard library can differ from the release of the same series.

rzig 0.3.5

Build files

  • The generated Makevars compile src/entry.c with R’s compiler flags ($(ALL_CFLAGS)), so the flags of the R installation and of CRAN’s check configurations reach it; the fixed -O2 -Wall -pedantic is gone.
  • zig build runs with -j2, within CRAN’s limit of two cores during checks.
  • configure asks R for its include directory (R.home("include")), which Linux distributions can place outside R_HOME, and falls back to R_HOME/include.
  • The macOS repack script points TMPDIR at its own temporary directory, so a cache written by the Apple tool shims (xcrun_db) is removed with it and does not appear as detritus in R CMD check.

rzig 0.3.4

Documentation

  • The help pages render their Markdown: DESCRIPTION declares Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE), so links between the step functions, the bullet lists of ?rzig_status and code spans appear as intended instead of as literal [build_zig()], **DESCRIPTION** and backticks.

rzig 0.3.3

Bug fixes

  • Reinstalling a client package from its source folder (R CMD INSTALL, install.packages(path, repos = NULL), the RStudio Install button) rebuilt the Zig library only when build.zig, build.zig.zon or main.zig changed, so an edit of any other Zig file, or of the framework, left the old native code in the package. The generated Makevars now runs zig build on every installation; Zig’s cache keeps an unchanged build fast.
  • use_rzig() lists the Zig sources in the Config/build/extra-sources field of DESCRIPTION (keeping entries the package author listed), so devtools::load_all() recompiles after a change to a Zig file instead of loading the old shared object.
  • rzig_status() notes a DESCRIPTION whose SystemRequirements does not name Zig or whose Config/build/extra-sources does not list the Zig sources. A DESCRIPTION without a Version field no longer stops the check with “subscript out of bounds”.

rzig 0.3.2

Bug fixes

  • rzig_status() compares only the framework sources under src/rzig/framework with the installed rzig. build.zig, build.zig.zon and src/rzig/tools/ are templates a package may extend, like configure and the Makevars, so a difference is a note and no longer fails the Scaffold check; build_zig() therefore builds packages with customized build files. A missing build file still fails the check. src/entry.c is compared with its template after the package name is substituted.

rzig 0.3.1

Bug fixes

  • The generated .Call wrappers are no longer symbols of the client package’s shared object. Each wrapper was exported under the R name of its function, so an export named like a C library function (exp, log, free) replaced that function inside the package and crashed R at the first call. The wrappers are reached through the registration table only, and rzig_init has hidden visibility; the shared object exports only R_init_<pkg> and R_unload_<pkg>.
  • rzig_status() notes an export that masks a function of base R or of the attached base packages, for example log.

rzig 0.3.0

Step-wise workflow

  • New functions expose each step of the workflow: find_zig() locates a supported Zig compiler, scan_exports() lists the exported Zig functions with their R arguments and the R values of every parameter and return type, render_bindings() shows the generated manifest, R wrappers and NAMESPACE block, and rzig_status() reports which steps of a package are complete and whether the generated bindings match the Zig source.
  • build_zig() compiles and installs a package from a temporary copy, keeps the complete installation log, and reports the errors of the Zig compiler, the C compiler, the linker and the load test with their files and lines, and the exported function concerned.
  • rzig_status() checks, before compilation, argument and return types the boundary rejects, more than 32 arguments, misuse of rzig.Mut([]f64), error sets other than rzig.Error, the registration block and panic handler in main.zig, R functions with the name of an export, framework sources from another rzig version, non-executable configure and cleanup scripts, and the C toolchain of R. rzig_status(build = TRUE) adds the result of build_zig().
  • use_rzig(overwrite = TRUE) updates the framework sources and build files and keeps the package author’s Zig sources in src/rzig/src. It adds the Zig build caches to .Rbuildignore.
  • use_rzig() and document() return printable objects describing the files written and the exports found.
  • The export scan runs in R. use_rzig(), scan_exports(), render_bindings() and document() need no Zig compiler; Zig is required only to install a package created with the scaffold. The package examples run on CRAN, and the vignette executes the generation steps.
  • The Zig scanner is no longer copied into client packages.

Zig version policy

  • rzig supports the Zig 0.16 and 0.17 release series. find_zig() and the generated configure scripts accept versions 0.16.x and 0.17.x and reject other series with a message naming the found version, because Zig changes its language and standard library between release series. The framework reads the type descriptions of both compilers and sets the Zig cache directories through environment variables, which both compilers accept.

Portability

  • The generated src/entry.c includes no R header. R installations whose headers lack R_ext/Visibility.h, such as the Debian and Ubuntu r-base packages, can install client packages.

Tests

  • tests/testthat runs on CRAN: scanner fixtures, rendering, the scaffold and documentation workflow without Zig, and find_zig(). A parity test compares the R scan with the Zig scanner where a supported Zig is present.

Licensing

  • rzig is distributed under GPL-3. Releases up to and including 0.2.3 remain available under the MIT license.
  • The example package rzigcausal and the test package rzigtest are distributed under GPL-3.

rzig 0.2.3

CRAN release: 2026-09-12

CRAN resubmission

  • Removed redundant wording from the package title and description.
  • use_rzig() and document() now require an explicit package path, so neither function writes to the working directory by default.
  • Added executable, temporary-directory examples for both exported functions; they use \donttest{} because they require the external Zig toolchain.
  • document() now confines Zig’s local and global caches to an automatically cleaned R session temporary directory. On Unix, its compiler subprocess also receives a private temporary directory.

rzig 0.2.2

CRAN submission

  • Updated the maintainer contact and added the author’s ORCID identifier.

rzig 0.2.1

Package authoring

  • use_rzig() now scaffolds cleanup and cleanup.win, preventing generated Makevars and Zig build caches from entering source-package checks.
  • document() uses the same Zig discovery order as package configuration and rejects unsupported compiler versions before running the export scanner.
  • The onboarding guide now edits the generated example in place, documents the complete parameter and return surface, and explains warning and roxygen2 workflows.

rzig 0.2.0

Statistical interface breadth

  • Integer, logical, and character vectors can be returned directly, decorated with attributes, and placed in generated lists.
  • Ctx.rng() provides boundary-managed draws from R’s random-number stream, preserving set.seed() reproducibility on success and error paths.
  • Rmath.normalCdf() and Rmath.normalQuantile() expose the linked R runtime’s normal distribution functions without consuming random state.

Boundary behavior

  • User interrupts retain R’s interrupt condition class after Zig cleanup; ordinary error handlers and try() no longer swallow Ctrl-C.
  • The POSIX integration gate sends a real SIGINT, checks the condition class, and verifies that the R session remains usable.
  • The causal demonstration now returns a logical adjacency matrix and covers all three-variable orders plus a 12-variable search through depth five.

rzig 0.1.0

Package authoring

  • use_rzig() scaffolds a portable Zig-backed R package, including generated registration, build configuration, and a working native example.
  • document() derives R wrappers, exports, and documentation from plain Zig functions marked with /// @export.
  • Generated packages build on Linux, macOS, and Windows with Zig 0.16.0 and R’s platform toolchain.

Native interface

  • Typed conversions cover numeric, integer, logical, optional, string, vector, list, matrix, attributed, and explicitly mutable values.
  • Mutable numeric inputs follow R copy-on-modify semantics by duplicating before Zig receives writable storage.
  • Long computations can check R interrupts, and pure Zig indexed loops can use capability-restricted worker threads.

Reliability

  • Native errors and ReleaseSafe panics become R conditions after Zig cleanup has completed.
  • The boundary protects R allocations, keeps borrowed inputs read-only, and confines R API access to the calling thread.
  • Cross-platform checks include hostile-input tests, garbage-collection stress, valgrind, native interface analysis, and reproducible boundary benchmarks.

Documentation

  • Added a worked package tutorial and a vignette showing how to port an Rcpp hot loop while preserving copy-on-modify, error, and interrupt behavior.
